I am an old man, and this small plot near my home is the one I watch most carefully. At my age, I cannot walk far, so I tend this 0.09 hectare maize plot with help from my children and grandchildren. I will put both cow manure and a little bit of chemical fertilizer—what the extension agent calls DAP and urea—because this soil needs help, but I do not have money to waste. I will plant the maize seed I saved from last season, pull weeds by hand, and pray for rain, because I have no pump and no money for chemicals. My family will do most of the work, but I may hire a young man with oxen for a day or two when the land must be plowed.
